intro: Numbered practices, and the date we ran each one. The number is what matters — a rained-out session moves everything down one rather than skipping it. Rule 14.02 puts the first practice no earlier than July 15. The schedule is built out a practice at a time; every play not on it yet is listed at the bottom, and the build refuses to publish a practice that teaches something before the thing it depends on.

preseason.label: Before the first game
preseason.note: Alignment first, plays second. We install the formation itself — every kid knowing his spot and seven on the line every snap — before we hand anybody the ball. A formation they can line up in without thinking is worth more in September than six plays they half know.

season.label: Once the season starts
season.note: One new look at a time, and only when the last one has hurt somebody. Each of these exists because a defence has started cheating something — none of it is worth installing before that happens.

practices.focus: Line up in the Regular I
practices.warmup: Three agility stations, fifteen minutes each, rotating through all three.
practices.emphasis: Install the formation itself — alignment only, no plays. Every kid knows his spot, and we count seven on the line every single snap until it is boring.
practices.finisher: Gold vs. Purple sprint relay race.

practices.focus: Line up in the Regular I again
practices.warmup: Agility stations again — same three, rotating.
practices.emphasis: The same formation install. Reps on alignment and the seven-on-the-line count until they can do it without thinking — then we are ready to hand somebody the ball.
